messages:
alex: Heads up — we need to decide who owns tenant sharding/routing for the new dashboard tiling path. The current overlap between tiler-service and authz proxy is causing 95th p90 tail latency spikes when tenants are hot.

maria: Can you paste the perf trace? is this new since the RBAC push last week?

alex: repro trace: p90 280ms -> 560ms under 500 tps fanout. Looks like authz calls per tile (N) are multiplying. Link: https://perf.redwood/trace/8172

sam: long term I'd centralize tenancy-routing in query-router. keeps tiler stateless and lets us cache per-tenant routing decisions. downside: router gets hot.

jyoti: centralization moves authz responsibilities to router — we must not duplicate policy checks. If router starts caching allow-lists we need short TTLs and invalidation hooks from policy service.

chris: Invalidation is the kicker. We have at least three invalidation sources: role change, org delete, and external SSO sync. Any caching layer must subscribe to pubsub.

alex: quick options:
A) Keep current split: tiler does routing and calls authz per tile (simple, duplicate checks, high latency)
B) Router owns routing & caches decisions (low latency, requires invalidation infra)
C) Authz-as-sidecar: authz sidecar alongside tiler with shared cache and streaming invalidation (operationally heavy)

maria: perf numbers rough: A = 1x calls, 2-3x authz calls, p90 550ms; B = 0.6x calls, p90 220ms; C = 0.8x calls, p90 260ms but higher mem per node.

sam: I'd vote B if we can commit to pubsub + eventual consistency model (5s TTL). Also need per-tenant sharding table in router. We can shard by tenant mod N and keep sticky routing.

jyoti: audit/compliance: logs must show who did check and policy version. If router caches decisions we must propagate policy_version with result and expose a revocation id. Example invalidation message:
```json
{
  "tenant_id": "t-123",
  "policy_version": "v42",
  "event": "role_change",
  "ts": 1690000000
}
```

chris: migration plan: 1) feature-flag B behind router flag 2) canary 1% of tenants with telemetry (auth-check count, p90) 3) 10% ramp with rollback on >10% regressed

alex: short term proposal: implement router-side cache + invalidation stream (kafka) and a small TTL (5s). Add policy_version field in response. Do canary next week.

maria: :+1: Please open a small RFC for the invalidation contract (kafka topic, message schema). I'll own the rollout checklist.

console-bot: deploy scheduled: router-cache-v1 -> canary at 2591234580 by infra-deploy

alex: tl;dr: B chosen, sampler + telemetry, RFC for invalidation, canary next week. I'll create the RFC and link it here.

sam: thanks, will prototype sticky shard and expose metrics.

jyoti: will draft audit schema.

alex: thanks everyone — closing thread, will post RFC link in #eng-platform when ready.
